The Delete/Archive distinction is clear. Screenshots under `prototypes/` (live: **http://maker:4001/archive.html**).

**Archive and Delete side by side** (`shot-30-archive-with-delete.png`)
Each bookmark now shows two clearly different actions: **🗄 Archive** (neutral/amber — the reversible "tuck away") and a distinct **🗑 Delete** in red for permanent removal. Different colour, different icon, different wording, so they're not confused.

**Delete asks first** (`shot-31-delete-confirm.png`)
Clicking **Delete** opens a confirmation that names the bookmark, states plainly that it **cannot be undone** (bookmark, tags and note gone for good), and — crucially — nudges you toward Archive if you only wanted it out of the way: *"Just want it out of your main list? Use Archive instead — that keeps it and can be restored anytime."* You confirm with a red **Delete permanently**, or **Cancel**. Archive, by contrast, is a single click with no scary dialog because it's fully reversible.

So the full picture for this step:
- **Archive** hides a bookmark from the main To read / Finished / All views while **keeping its reading status**; it lives under the **Archived** entry and **Restore** returns it in the same state.
- **Delete** permanently removes it, gated by a confirmation, visibly separate from Archive.
- **Search:** archived bookmarks are excluded from ordinary searches; searching **from within the Archived view** searches only archived bookmarks.

Does this fully match your intent for archiving and deletion? If yes, I'll record it and we'll move to the **last piece — saving the same link twice taking you to the existing bookmark instead of making a duplicate.**
